dispute_ticket.description: He dropped me at Block 21 Toa Payoh Lor 1, about 300 m from my booked drop-off at Block 25, and I had to walk in the rain with shopping bags. I would like S$3 back. Also, the next morning he messaged me on the app saying he liked my red dress and asking me out for coffee this weekend, and when I said no he said he would message again tomorrow. I never gave him any reason to.

chat_logs.content: Traffic light ahead, I drop you at Lor 1 side ok?
Hi, it's Kelvin from last night. You looked lovely in that red dress. Can I take you for coffee this weekend?
No thank you. Please do not message me.
Just one coffee! I'll message you again tomorrow

app_events.details: Trip completed at GPS 1.3375, 103.8505 (about 300 m from booked drop-off); fare S$12.30.

dropoff_tolerance_m.text: Governs drop-off disputes. A drop-off further than this many metres from the booked point, without the rider's agreement, may justify a refund.

drop_off_short_refund.text: The SGD amount refunded when the driver drops the rider off outside the tolerance without agreement.

post_trip_personal_contact_prohibited.text: Governs a driver contacting a rider after the trip for personal reasons. A true value means such contact is not allowed.

refund_at_ryde_discretion.text: Governs refunds on this trip. A true value means Ryde may refund beyond the strict rules where the facts justify it. It does not create a right to a refund.

expected_outcome.reason: The drop-off complaint is ordinary and partly answered by the chat (the driver asked at 20:50:30 to drop at the Lor 1 side and the rider replied 'ok fine' at 20:50:45, so agreement is arguable). The matter that decides routing is the contact after the trip: at 11:42:00 the next day the driver messages her about her red dress and asks her out, she refuses at 11:44:10 and asks him not to message her, and at 11:45:00 he says he will message again tomorrow. This is a personal romantic advance by the driver that continues after a refusal, a safety matter that v2.1 s5.2 sends to a person, so no automated verdict or S$3 refund.
